claim.why_it_matters: A stray pair of markdown bold markers has been wrapped around the terminating period of the returned-value expression; nothing in the printed page is emphasized there. The raw text now reads '+ 1)**.**' inside an arithmetic expression, and '**' is COBOL's exponentiation operator, so a reader or extraction tool taking the expression verbatim can misparse it. The sibling occurrence in 15.94.4 c) on page 958 is transcribed correctly as '(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1).'.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed on both sides, and the claim quotes both sources exactly. MARKDOWN: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 38466 (inside the page-961 block that opens at line 38456) reads verbatim '(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1)**.**'. PDF: the 300dpi render of PDF page 961 (printed page 931, 15.95.4 TEST-NUMVAL-F Returned value rule, item c) shows '(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1).' in uniform regular-weight serif; the terminating period is visually identical in weight to the other periods on the page. Independent glyph-level confirmation from the PDF font runs (PyMuPDF rawdict, page index 960): the expression line at y=229.6 is a SINGLE span, font 'Cambria', size 10.70, flags=4 (serif, bold bit 16 clear) covering the whole line including the period. The ONLY bold run anywhere on page 961 is the running header at y=37.8 ('Cambria,Bold', flags=20), which the markdown correctly renders as '**ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)**'. So there is no font-weight or emphasis change at the period for the converter to have been representing; the '**' pair is inserted noise with no counterpart in the source. The claim's corroborating detail also checks out: the two sibling transcriptions of the identical sentence -- line 38324 (15.93.4 TEST-NUMVAL, page 957) and line 38393 (15.94.4 TEST-NUMVAL-C, page 958) -- are both plain '(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1).', which proves the emphasis on page 961 is one-off OCR noise rather than a transcription convention. Rejection triggers checked and none apply: the text is not merely reflowed or on an adjacent line (it is present, with extra characters); this is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation; neither source is misquoted. It is filed as cosmetic, which is the correct severity -- no normative content is added, lost, or altered, and a markdown renderer displays the same sentence -- but four asterisk characters absent from the canonical page have been injected into the raw text of a normative arithmetic expression, so it is a genuine transcription defect and belongs in the ledger at cosmetic priority. Fix is a one-character-class edit: delete the two '**' pairs on line 38466.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as filed, with one rationale caveat. Confirmed: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 38466 has '(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1)**.**' where PDF page 961 (printed 931, 15.95.4 c) has plain '(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1).'; font-run inspection shows the line is one non-bold Cambria span and the page's only bold run is its running header, so the emphasis is pure OCR noise -- consistent with the two identical sentences at lines 38324 (15.93.4, page 957) and 38393 (15.94.4, page 958), both transcribed plain. Caveat on the stated impact: the practical risk is narrower than 'a reader can misparse it' suggests -- rendered markdown shows the same sentence and no normative content changes, so the exposure is limited to tooling that greps the RAW markdown for the returned-value expression and would capture '+ 1)**.**', where '**' collides with COBOL's exponentiation operator. Cosmetic severity is correct.
